description: Batch A of Mock Exam 6: author AND evaluate 30 original BABOK v3-based CBAP questions (working ids 1-30) as a self-contained unit, then gate on a quality/difficulty evaluation before accepting. This is the FIRST of four batches; the user explicitly wants 30-at-a-time authoring with a genuine per-batch quality/difficulty evaluation rather than a 120-at-once bulk generation. Also folds in trivial environment setup (confirm branch, load dedup corpus). Save the accepted 30 items to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchA.json (working area; not the final file yet). Coverage focus for Batch A (to be balanced across all four batches): BA Planning & Monitoring and Elicitation & Collaboration weighted, with a couple of Techniques items.
steps: Confirm you are on branch add-mock-exam-6 (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD). Do NOT re-create it; it already exists off up-to-date main.

Read the existing mock5 (and skim mock4) set objects in js/data/questions.json (BOM-aware: python encoding='utf-8-sig', or in node strip a leading 0xFEFF then JSON.parse) to lock in exact schema and writing style: set keys [categoryId, categoryName, questions, setName, totalQuestions]; question keys [answer, choices, explanation, id, question]; choices object A/B/C/D; explanations BABOK-grounded and note why distractors are wrong; financial items carry full worked arithmetic in the explanation.

Programmatically extract all 1650 existing question stems from js/data/questions.json into a normalized dedup corpus (lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace). Save this corpus building script under .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/ so later batches reuse it.

Author 30 NEW, original, scenario-driven CBAP questions grounded in BABOK v3 with fresh people/organizations/situations. Each: exactly four non-empty options A-D and exactly one best (defensible BABOK-correct) answer, plus a BABOK-grounded explanation that justifies the key and rules out the three distractors. Distractors must be plausible-but-wrong (no throwaway/absurd options unless a deliberately easy item).

Label a target difficulty per item (medium / difficult / very difficult) and deliberately calibrate toward ~25% medium (~7-8), ~50% difficult (~15), ~25% very difficult (~7-8) within this batch of 30.

EVALUATE THE BATCH before accepting (this is the gate, not optional): for each of the 30 items verify (a) exactly one defensible BABOK-correct answer and three plausible distractors; (b) stem is unambiguous and self-contained; (c) the batch actually hits the ~25/50/25 difficulty mix (tally the per-item labels and confirm — if it drifted all-easy, revise items up); (d) each explanation justifies the key AND rules out distractors; (e) coverage note for how this batch contributes to the overall six-KA + competencies/techniques/perspectives distribution. Revise any weak item in place until the whole batch passes.

Run an internal + external dedup check on the 30: normalize each new stem; confirm none matches or near-matches any of the 1650 existing stems (flag high token-overlap and identical option phrasing too), and none duplicates another item within the batch. Replace near-duplicates with fresh originals; iterate to 0.

Honesty: present content as original authoring grounded in BABOK v3 general knowledge; do NOT claim it matches any unseen external source. If a single item leans on a specific BABOK term/section/number you cannot verify, append '[verify against your BABOK reference]' to that item's explanation.
Save the 30 accepted items as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchA.json (working ids 1-30; do NOT touch js/data/questions.json yet).

Record the batch findings in this feature JSON: the achieved difficulty mix (counts of medium/difficult/very-difficult), the KA/coverage spread, per-batch A/B/C/D answer tally, confirmation the evaluation gate passed, and confirmation dedup ran with 0 duplicates (external + internal).
acceptance_criteria: .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchA.json exists and parses as a JSON array of exactly 30 question objects.
Each item has keys answer, choices, explanation, id, question; choices has non-empty A,B,C,D; answer in {A,B,C,D}; explanation non-empty.
Per-item difficulty labels tally to roughly 25% medium / 50% difficult / 25% very difficult and this is recorded in findings.
Batch evaluation gate is recorded in findings: single defensible answer per item, plausible distractors, unambiguous stems, explanations that rule out distractors, coverage note.
Dedup reports 0 duplicates/near-dupes for the 30 vs the 1650 existing stems and 0 internal duplicates within the batch.
js/data/questions.json and js/app.js are NOT modified by this feature (batch work stays in the batches/ working area).
verification: python3/node: load batches/batchA.json; assert length==30; assert each item has 4 non-empty A-D choices, answer in ABCD, non-empty explanation, unique ids.
python3/node dedup script: rebuild normalized corpus from all existing questions (1650); assert 0 batchA stems match; assert 0 internal duplicates within batchA.
Read findings and confirm the difficulty-mix tally and evaluation-gate notes are present.
git diff --stat main -- js/data/questions.json js/app.js shows no changes from this feature.
findings:
Batch A complete: 30 original scenario-driven BABOK v3 questions authored, evaluated, and saved as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchA.json (working ids 1-30). Reusable dedup tool saved at .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/dedup_corpus.py (builds normalized corpus from all existing stems, checks exact/near-dup via Jaccard>=0.75, identical-option-set phrasing, and internal dups). NOTE: I added a non-schema 'difficulty' key to each item in batchA.json to carry the per-item difficulty label used for the evaluation gate; this working-area key must be stripped during FEAT-005 compile before appending to js/data/questions.json (the production schema is answer/choices/explanation/id/question only).

ENVIRONMENT: confirmed on branch add-mock-exam-6 (off up-to-date main). Existing corpus verified as 26 sets / 1650 questions, read BOM-aware (utf-8-sig). js/data/questions.json and js/app.js NOT modified by this feature (all work in batches/ working area).

ACHIEVED DIFFICULTY MIX: medium=8 (27%), difficult=15 (50%), very difficult=7 (23%) -> hits the ~25/50/25 target. First draft drifted easy (10 medium / 5 very difficult); the evaluation gate caught this and I revised two medium items UP into genuinely harder discrimination items (id5 reframed around influence-vs-impact classification of a supportive low-authority manager; id16 reframed to require matching each of three information types to its authoritative source under schedule pressure) rather than merely relabeling.

KA / COVERAGE SPREAD (Batch A weighting = BA Planning & Monitoring + Elicitation & Collaboration, plus a couple of Techniques items, per plan): BA Planning & Monitoring (KA1): ids 1,2,3,4,5,7,18,19,20,25,26,27 (~12 items covering plan approach, plan stakeholder engagement/stakeholder analysis, plan information management, plan governance/approval authority, business analysis risk, traceability planning, estimation, performance monitoring, assumptions/constraints, requirements reuse). Elicitation & Collaboration (KA2): ids 8,9,10,11,12,13,15,21,24,28,30 (~11 items covering prepare for elicitation, conduct elicitation via observation/workshop, confirm elicitation results, manage stakeholder collaboration, source selection, adapting technique, professional objectivity under stakeholder pressure, right-sizing effort). Techniques (Ch10): ids 14 (document analysis), 17 (decision analysis) plus observation/facilitated-workshop technique reasoning embedded in 9 and 13. Strategy-analysis financial calculation items: ids 22 (simple payback) and 23 (present value comparison) with FULL worked arithmetic in their explanations (both verified numerically: id22 payback = 2 + 210,000/280,000 = 2.75 yrs; id23 X pv = 50,000/1.08 = 46,296, Y pv = 55,000/1.1664 = 47,154, so Y higher). Overall balance across the four KAs / competencies / techniques / perspectives is planned to complete across batches B-D.

PER-BATCH A/B/C/D ANSWER TALLY: A=7, B=8, C=8, D=7 (balanced; well-positioned for the mock4/mock5-style 30/30/30/30 target once all 120 are compiled).

EVALUATION GATE PASSED (verified item-by-item): (a) each item has exactly one defensible BABOK-correct answer and three plausible-but-wrong distractors (no throwaway/absurd options); (b) every stem is self-contained and unambiguous; (c) the batch verifiably hits the ~25/50/25 difficulty mix after upward revision; (d) every explanation justifies the key AND explicitly rules out the three distractors; (e) coverage note recorded above. Schema validation script passed: 30 items, ids 1-30 unique, all choices A-D non-empty and mutually distinct, answer in {A,B,C,D}, explanation non-empty.

DEDUP CONFIRMATION: dedup_corpus.py built a 1650-stem normalized corpus from js/data/questions.json (BOM-aware) and reported 0 exact duplicates, 0 near-duplicates (Jaccard>=0.75), 0 identical-option-set matches vs existing, and 0 internal duplicates within Batch A. A lowered-threshold sanity pass showed only the two financial items (id22, id23) exceed 0.5 Jaccard vs existing financial questions, driven by shared formulaic vocabulary (investment/inflows/discount rate/present value); their scenarios, numbers, and answers are all distinct, so they are legitimately original standard-type calculation items, not duplicates.

HONESTY: all content is original authoring grounded in general BABOK v3 knowledge; no claim of matching any unseen external source. No item required a '[verify against your BABOK reference]' tag because none leans on a specific unverifiable BABOK section/number; concepts referenced (Plan Business Analysis Approach, Plan Stakeholder Engagement, Plan/Manage governance, Prepare for/Conduct/Confirm Elicitation, Manage Stakeholder Collaboration, decision analysis, document analysis, observation, facilitated workshop, simple payback, present value) are standard BABOK v3 knowledge-area and technique concepts.
